title: AI Governance and Assurance
subtitle: Standards and frameworks written for artificial intelligence itself
body_html:
These are the standards and frameworks written for artificial intelligence itself. Some are management systems an organisation can be certified against, such as ISO/IEC 42001. Some are risk frameworks it can adopt voluntarily, such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its generative AI profile. Others define the vocabulary, catalogue the attacks on AI systems, or set out principles that governments have agreed to. None of them has legal force on its own, but laws, regulators and contracts increasingly point to them, and the EU AI Act relies on harmonised standards such as EN 18286 to show conformity. Each page says what the standard covers, who issues it, how a claim to follow it is checked, and what a claim does not mean.

Management systems and risk

  • ISO/IEC 42001
    The AI Management System Standard
  • NIST AI Risk Management Framework
    Govern, Map, Measure, Manage
  • NIST AI 600-1
    The companion to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework for generative AI, released July 2024
  • ISO/IEC 23894
    The guidance standard that applies ISO 31000 risk management to AI, published 2023
  • ISO/IEC 42005
    The guidance standard for assessing how an AI system affects people and society, published 2025
  • IEEE 2863-2026
    IEEE's recommended practice for how a governing body directs and oversees AI
  • EN 18286:2026
    The first harmonised standard under the EU AI Act, for the Article 17 quality management system

Vocabulary, threats and testing

  • ISO/IEC 22989
    AI Vocabulary Standard
  • ISO/IEC 27090:2026
    Guidance on security threats and compromises to AI systems
  • MITRE ATLAS
    The adversary tactics and techniques knowledge base for attacks on AI systems
  • AI Assurance Standards
    Which kind of assurance proves what

Intergovernmental principles

  • OECD AI Principles
    The 2019 intergovernmental standard on trustworthy AI, revised in 2024, adopted by 47 jurisdictions
  • UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
    The 2021 global standard adopted by all 193 UNESCO member states
  • G7 Hiroshima AI Process Code of Conduct
    The 2023 G7 guiding principles and code of conduct for organizations developing advanced AI
